utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us, where did you graduate from university and when, with your major in geography?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I graduated in 1976 in Prishtina. I graduated from the Faculty of Natural Sciences for Geography.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I noticed in your statement that between 1981 and 1985 you worked in Germany. What type of jobs did you have there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: From 1991 [as interpreted] to 1985 I worked as a teacher in Germany for four years. I worked with the Albanian kids, teaching them from the first grade to the high school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us just exactly what years were you in Germany from for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] From 1981 to 1985. I can tell you either in Serbian or in Albanian, you choose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, were these state schools in Germany where you taught Albanian children there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] It was kind of supplementary teaching in Albanian. We were simply complementing their programme. It was done for the Albanian population living in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you were employed by -- who financed your employment, the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It was -- I was financed by Kosova Community of Education plus a part was financed by the German government.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you returned from Germany, did you start working in a state school in Decani?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: They had kept my place of work in this high school called Brothers Frasheri in Decan. I returned and resumed to work immediately until 1991 when we were dismissed together with 135 teachers and 2.550 students. And then after that, we continued teaching in private homes, make-shift facilities, in villages that the villagers made available for us. They drove us away from schools. And this school, which was in an area of 5.200 square metres, was used only for 36 students of Montenegrin ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After 1990 were you a member of a political party?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I used to be a member of the political party of Ibrahim Rugova, LDK.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you an official for your village or the Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I was never an official. I was simply a professor in my village. I have taken care of my village. After the first offensive, I had 520 members in my village. I took care of the 37 members of Sllup family. I took care of them to provide as much assistance as I could to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it fair to say that you were the elder of the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Could you please repeat?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that you were the elder of the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: We didn't have that title in the village at the time. We don't have it now either. Families remained in our village, children, elderly, women, who needed help; and I tried to provide them with as much assistance as possible, distributed humanitarian aid to them, and protected them to the extent that I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraphs 6 and 7 of your statement you say that there were in the village six Serbian families and that they left in 1998. Did they later return?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It is true that these families, Montenegrin families, lived in my village. Four of these families lived near the primary school; another house, the Zecevic -- Jovan Zecevic's family lived in my neighbourhood; and there was another family, Mijatovic family, who left the village very early. They left the village because of economic reasons. When the war broke out, the other families left the village and moved to apartments in Decan under the pretext of being able to protect themselves better, but their aim was to appropriate apartments there. They had no problems whatsoever from our side. We looked after their cattle and even when they came back from the town of Decan to tend to their cattle in the village, we didn't cause them any harm. They could freely come back and return to Decan whenever they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1999, in March, were these families in the village or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: These Serbian families, were they in the village in March 1999 when the war began?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: They were in Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazrekaj, in paragraph 8 - and we're still talking about 1998 - you talk about a hill called Podi i Geshtenjane, excuse my pronunciation. Can you recognise what hill I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It is true that it is a forest there, but the area is called -- the hill is called Podi i Geshtenjane. That's where the police and the military were positioned together with their police and military artillery and equipment. And from there they were shelling in the direction of our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where is that hill?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Podi i Geshtenjane is near the children resort north-west from Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how far is it from your village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: From my village or from Decan?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From your village.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] 3 kilometres or so. [Albanian interpretation] Maybe more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is your village to the south of Decani?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: From Decan my village would be to the south-west of Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And how many kilometres is it from your village to Decani?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Three and a half kilometres approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And from Decani to the hill?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: About 1 kilometre. It's a hill just above Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were you able to see the artillery from your village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: No, I didn't have binoculars. It's a mountain, it's a forest, and the name itself, Podi i Geshtenjane, indicates that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I call up D002-4026. Could we zoom in on the area of Decani. Exactly. Perhaps zoom in a little. That's Decani.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here is Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in once again so the witness can mark his village and some other villages I'm interested in. They're all on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Decan, here is Drenoc. Decan, Drenoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mazrekaj. This dot you marked, which place is that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Just above Drenoc here is Lloqan, then you have Hulaj and then Pobergje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is Locane which you marked in red?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: [B/C/S interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that's on the other road going to Decani, the one going to Junik, and Drenovci is on the other road?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: [Albanian interpretation] Yes, you're right that village is on the road that takes you to Junik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... thank you. And this dot where Drenovac is, could you put a circle around it and a number 1.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I cannot see it clearly, Drenoc, because Lloqan and Drenoc seem to share the same dot.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let the image remain, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazrekaj, you cannot orient yourself on this map and mark it precisely, but let the map stay so that at least the rest of us can see the places marked there. Mr. Mazrekaj, how did you find out that the air-strikes started?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I saw that from my village, the shells landing in the direction of my village and other villages, Hulaj, Pobergje, and other villages from Podi i Geshtenjane. There was uninterrupted shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When was that, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: On the 29th of May, when Decan was bombed for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You're talking about 1998, whereas I'm asking you about 1999. How did you find out that the war began in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I was in the village when the war began.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you did not see this incident when Locane was set on fire?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Lloqan is 1 kilometre far from my village. The village is situated on the south-western part. To the north of the village we could not move freely because of the police orders of the time. I was in my home, and it was impossible to observe what was going on up there. Therefore, I didn't know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. But with regard to paragraph 28, you've already told me who was in the car with you. But when you got to Crnobreg, you were intercepted and stopped by the police. And when you told them that there were 520 families who wanted to go to Rznic [as interpreted] village, they let you pass. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: This was the second time that I went to Carrabreg to ask for permission. They surrounded us immediately. I asked Mr. Zoran kindly. I said to him, I'm here to ask you whether it would be possible for me and the 520 people in the village and the 37 people from Sllup to pass through here. He said, Yes. But when I returned in the village and spoke to the villagers, we realised that it was dangerous because there were many incidents when men were being separated from the women and the children, and that's why we didn't trust them. We couldn't go through that check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Please don't hold it against me, but is it worth putting perhaps the statement on the screen? Would you be able to read the statement from the screen so you can explain certain things more easily. If you can't read it then I won't ask for the statement to be displayed, then we could move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want to retain this image on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Then we'll put it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This image cannot be evidence. If I want to clarify something, I would ask for the witness's assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you understand me, Mr. Mazrekaj? Is it worth the trouble of putting the statement in Albanian on the screen? Would you be able to, with your glasses, to read it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I have the hard copy of my statement here in my bag, but if you want me to read, it I'll do my best to read it from the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You know why? I think because -- I think we are getting more and more confused. When I say paragraph 27 or 28 that's page 5 in Serbian. That's the first time you were going to Beleg village and reaching the police check-point. It's not the second time when you spoke to them about those 520 families. That's the first time you were going to Beleg from your village. Now I'd like to ask you: Why did you not lead the villagers as you had agreed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: There was no agreement. We all knew what was going to happen, and this happened later on, on the 30th, in Beleg. We didn't trust the police. That's why we didn't dare go through the check-point there at Carrabreg.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The two of you who were going to inquire were allowed to return by the police?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: They allowed us to return because we told them that we were going to come back with the remaining population through that check-point. They were ready to separate us from our women and children and to loot us, and this is what happened with many other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why then did you go to that check-point to inquire?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Because we thought that they would behave properly towards us, like humans, not like animals.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You go on to say in your statement that you went via Prilep to Beleg village, and in that village the locals told you that 18 Serbian soldiers had been killed. I'd like to ask you: Were you told where these Serbian soldiers were killed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: No. The villagers didn't say anything to us about this killing. Zoran Djurisic told us about this. He knew me very well. He said to me, Professor, your students killed us at Pozhar village, and we don't even dare and go and collect the bodies in Pozhar. He was the one who told me about this, not the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to see page 5 of the Albanian statement, please. Page 5 of the English version, third paragraph from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To speed things up, please look at the screen while I read. "The locals of Beleg told us to stay because 18 Serbian soldiers had been killed and the roads were therefore blocked." Is this statement accurate?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: This is what they knew. They were informed about this. The road was blocked towards Lumbardh and Dashinoc and that's why we stopped at Beleg that night because it was impossible to proceed. We went to different houses where we could find shelter and room for the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please give me brief answers. Did they tell you where the soldiers had been killed or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: No, just that gun-fire was heard because there was a confrontation with the KLA forces in Pozhar village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me if you know how the KLA came to be in Pozar village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: I don't know what happened there that night. I wasn't there. I know that the villagers of Pozhar saw that. The police then took the anger out at the population, civilian population that lived in their own houses in that village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It is the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What do you know about that army?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It was a liberation army of the state of Kosova, now state of Kosova, that fought for the rights of the Albanians in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How was this struggle by the KLA carried out?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: They know best. I didn't take part in that struggle. They know best how they fought.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this is the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. We will have our second adjournment now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazrekaj, you've said today that you were in another house, in a different house, and not in Xhafer Zukaj's house. In your 2000 statement in paragraphs 36, 39, 43, and 46 you mentioned the basement of Xhafer Zukaj's house, and only later you say that in the evening or toward the evening you moved to another house to the second floor, I believe this was in paragraph 52 and 53 of your statement. Now, what I don't understand now is - and please explain it - when the police detained you that second time, didn't they keep you in the basement in that house and wasn't all this happening in the situation where these police actually detained you, stopped you from going anywhere, or was it different?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: The police didn't detain me from going to another place. At Zukaj's house, the police were situated. The military were around it. Beleg is not my village, it's another village; but I was informed that in the house which was not fully completed, constructed, that belonged to Rram Cenaj [phoen] where we were staying in that basement. When they took us out, and in the evening when they put us in the second floor, to make it clear to you, we were not in the basement of Zukaj but in the basement of Rram Cenaj's [phoen] house as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now please tell us, this second time when you travelled to Crnobreg from Beleg village, in other words you were in Beleg, and then nine of you, and you were the tenth, set off for Crnobreg. How did you do this?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: It's not true that we went from Beleg to Carrabreg. We went from Drenoc to Carrabreg on the second time. I don't think it's written in my statement that we went from Beleg to Carrabreg.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that after this second time when you returned from Crnobreg, you actually went to Beleg?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: When I returned from Carrabreg I went to my own village. Together with the other inhabitants, we set off for Beleg from Drenoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mazrekaj, in paragraph 29 you say: "When I arrived in Drenoc," in other words that was on that first occasion when you returned when you said that this Zoran was going to wait for you at the check-point, you returned through Drenoc from Crnobreg and then via Prilep you went to Beleg and then you go on to talk about Beleg. And then you say that the villagers - and this is in paragraph 36 - asked you and specifically Male Vishaj, Sheqer Mazrekaj, Shaban Idrizalaj, Shaban Nitaj, Ise Tolaj, Mehmet Tolaj, and Misin Tolaj that you were to go to Xhafer Zukaj's house.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, we went that morning to ask the police where we could go from Beleg village with these people, which road to take to go to Isniq.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I didn't make myself clear, Mr. Mazrekaj. On the first occasion you went by car with another person whose name you mentioned, and this was described in paragraph 27 and paragraph 28 of your statement. And all these other nine or ten individuals that are named who went to you on another occasion again to Xhafer Zukaj's house, this is in paragraph 36. Was that -- this what I was reading from the statement correct or not, please just tell us.

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: You have not understood correctly. For the first and second time I left from Drenoc for Carrabreg. You are mixing up Beleg here. I said several times that we went that morning to inquire from the police to let -- to ask them to allow us to leave the village because that was on the 29th when we went.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, here in your statement in paragraph 32 mention is made of Sunday, the 28th of March; and in paragraph 28, the portion that I read the first time, you say that they let me return to the village and they said that they would wait for us there. And then paragraph 29: "When I arrived in Drenoc, I told the villagers not to go through Carrabreg because they would separate men from women and children. That was the reason why we passed through the village of Prilep to go to the village of Beleg. It was around 4.00 p.m. when we arrived in Beleg and there we were told about those 18 soldiers." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: This happened on the 27th, when we arrived in Beleg, on the 27th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But then in paragraph 31 you say: "Nothing happened that night in the village, but we could hear shooting in the surrounding villages." And then in the next paragraph, paragraph 32, you say: "On Sunday, the 28th of March, 1999, around 1.30 to 2.00 the police forces came."

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: The police came on the 28th to the village to check, to search the village, and some Qazim Hulaj was killed from the Hulaj family of Berber, and I didn't see him myself but he was killed. He was buried in Beleg. We others managed to escape and to go to the houses where we lived in Beleg.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that your wife and your parents remained in Adem Vishaj's house, as you state in paragraph 56 of your statement and that Sadik Vishaj told you about it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That is where they stayed, my wife, my father, mother, and a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And were they in Beleg village, in this house of Adem Vishaj's?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: They were at Adem Vishaj's home. There was nowhere they could go, but Adem Vishaj's family was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where is Adem Vishaj's house, in what village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: In Beleg. Where else?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where is Xhafer Zukaj's house?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: In Beleg too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Mazrekaj. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. My cross is complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. Just very briefly by way of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I just wanted to clear something up with respect to the chief of police. You gave us the name of the chief of police earlier in your testimony. I notice at page 33 of the transcript it was recorded as Bula, B-u-l-a, and I know that in cross-examination it was recorded as Vula, the nickname. Can you tell us which is correct, which is -- which is the name that you used?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: The correct name of the chief is Vukmir, Vula is the pseudonym, Mircic is the last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And that's Vula with a V then?

utterances.speaker: MEHMET MAZREKAJ
utterances.text: Vula is his pseudonym, Vula, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Those are all my questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be pleased to know that concludes the questioning for you. The Chamber is conscious that you've been to The Hague more than once. We are grateful that you've been able to come this further time to assist us. We have your evidence, your statement, and your previous transcript of evidence, and we will weigh all of that in due course. So we thank you, and you may of course now return to your normal activities, and the court officer will assist you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to thank you and wish you success in your work, and I wish that you are fair in your judgement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, I'm going to be asking if we could begin with Mr. Shaqiri, who's our next witness, on the next day. I have spoken with Mr. Neuner, who is leading Mr. Shaqiri. I understand there is some new material that's been provided that has just now been provided to the Defence. I understand that we do anticipate making an application to add that material to our exhibit list, and of course the Defence should have time to review it. I note there's about 25 minutes, but I would be making that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we assume there'll be no difficulty completing his evidence tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I don't believe so. If I could just have a moment's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yeah, I certainly don't anticipate any issues from our standpoint, and I don't know about the length of cross-examination, but I expect that he should be able to finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're listed for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So we certainly shouldn't run the whole day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well you shouldn't. Mr. Djurdjic, do you have any problem with the proposal to commence the final witness for this week tomorrow, and do you foresee any problem with completing the evidence tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't foresee any problems to finish with this witness tomorrow. Whether there will be some problems with the additional material, that remains to be seen, but I leave it up to you to decide on the request made by the Prosecution. But we certainly will complete our cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar, the Chamber is becoming increasingly concerned that we need to keep the case moving, and you will recall, no doubt, that only earlier this week we were not prepared to finish early on one day. In this case, however, we note that your reason is that there is to be notice of additional material to the Defence and there may be a motion for the addition of material to your exhibits. In that situation, we think that we can, therefore, grant your request and adjourn now. It will not be the practice of the Tribunal to be doing that in this trial, but we will on this occasion. And we do so in the expectation that the evidence will undoubtedly conclude tomorrow. So we now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 29th day of April, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.22 p.m.,
